To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the use of visual information in an AV-ASR system improves the performance of the acoustic model in noisy environments; (b) the use of a bottleneck network for visual modality improves the convergence of the fusion RNN; (c) the use of fusion RNNs for AV-ASR gives better results as compared to feature fusion; and (d) the use of CTC objective function for acoustic model helps in improving the performance of the AV-ASR model.

the use of visual features in an AV-ASR system can improve the performance of the acoustic model in noisy conditions and that a deep bottleneck network can be used to reduce the dimensionality of visual features.

the proposed method of using a bottleneck network for dimensionality reduction of visual features improves the convergence of the fusion RNN and that the fusion RNN trained using feature fusion outperforms the one trained using decision fusion.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of speech recognition in the presence of noise.
the problem of speech recognition in noisy environments.
the development of a deep RNN based AV-ASR system that can handle noisy speech and is robust to missing visual data.

our proposed system is robust to noise and can achieve significant improvement in performance when compared to the audio-only system.
the proposed method outperforms the baseline system and the state of the art methods in terms of character error rate (WER).
our proposed method is robust to noise.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the fusion RNN trained on audio and visual features using bottleneck features gives a better performance than the feature fusion RNN trained with the same features.
the proposed method is a promising approach to AV-ASR.
the fusion method has a significant effect on the recognition performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of visual modality helps in improving the performance of an AV-ASR system even when there is no access to noisy data during training.
a simple audio visual fusion system using deep RNN can be trained to give significant improvements in performance.
the proposed training algorithm is robust to noisy data and can be used to develop an AV-ASR system that can be trained on clean data and deployed on a noisy environment.
